comment: Enumerated triggers for the documentation-coupling check (F10/#256). GitLab-style: the rule is a committed list, not a slogan, so it can be audited and argued with. Docs are expected when a change introduces or enhances user-facing behavior, changes an interface, changes a documented process, or deprecates something. BACKEND-ONLY IS EXEMPT - that exemption is the reason the list below is short and specific rather than a catch-all on source paths.
sizing_note: The list starts deliberately small. A trigger that fires on everything teaches people to ignore the check, and this mechanism works only while its output is believed. Add a trigger when a real drift gets through, not in anticipation.
doc_globs_note: What COUNTS as documentation for the purposes of satisfying a trigger. change-specs/** counts: a change spec is where a normal- or high-tier change explains itself, and requiring a second document on top of it would be ceremony.

triggers.why: a user-facing command's flags or behavior
changes what happens inside a session without anyone asking
CI is a documented process; docs/BRANCH-PROTECTION.md describes it
a toggle is an interface: someone has to know it exists to use it
the files that decide how much scrutiny a change gets
mutates the machine outside the repo; the steps are documented

exempt_globs_note: A test-only diff is backend-only by definition. It also cannot introduce user-facing behavior, which is the first of the four documented conditions.
